reasoning: Consolidated the overlapping name-form guidance into one edit to the unprotected conventional-names section, distinguishing identifying name elements from merely descriptive ranks or honorifics. Added the distinct geographic-affiliation rule for bare proper-name pairs. Left the protected section unchanged.

edits.target: For proper names and titles, use the conventional form that identifies the requested entity. Do not substitute a nickname or later brand name for the historically relevant label, omit words from a work's title when the work is requested, or add optional middle names. Conversely, when the clue requests a generic class, do not embellish it with a narrower associated name.
edits.content: For proper names and titles, use the conventional designation for the entity in the historical or contextual frame asked about. Do not substitute a nickname or later brand name for the historically relevant label, or expand an established public name to a different formal given-name variant. Retain words intrinsic to a work's title when the work is requested, and avoid optional middle names. Include initials, titles, or other elements when they are part of the requested entity's conventional identifying name; do not append a rank, honorific, or status stated only as a description. Conversely, when the clue requests a generic class, do not embellish it with a narrower associated name.

edits.target: ## Check for Shared Completions in Parallel Clues
edits.content: For a bare pair of proper names separated by a comma, with no relation stated, treat the prompt as asking for a shared attribute. Use context to check for a specific common geographic affiliation, such as a state or country, before answering with a broad shared role. Return that place only when the context supports the link for both names; do not infer it from association alone.
